lineage: Closed operation that moved to an affiliate (RaaS) model in early 2023; unrelated to MedusaLocker
summary: Medusa is a double-extortion RaaS operation active since June 2021 that buys access from initial access brokers and rapidly weaponises newly disclosed edge/RMM CVEs (ScreenConnect, FortiClient EMS, GoAnywhere, BeyondTrust). Operators live off the land with heavily obfuscated PowerShell, rotate through many RMM tools and tunnels, kill EDR with signed malicious/vulnerable drivers (ABYSSWORKER, POORTRY/KillAV), and push the gaze.exe encryptor network-wide with PDQ Deploy.
uniqueTraits: Exploits newly published CVEs within ~24h (CVE-2024-1709, CVE-2023-48788, CVE-2025-10035, CVE-2026-1731) and verifies exploitation via Interactsh OOB domains
ABYSSWORKER driver (smuol.sys) masquerading as CrowdStrike CSAgent.sys, plus POORTRY/KillAV BYOVD, distributed with PDQ Deploy
PDQ Deploy playbook that excludes C:\ from Defender, robocopies gaze.exe into System32 and runs it
openrdp.bat pushed via PsExec (netsh RDP/WMI firewall rules + fDenyTSConnections=0)
mimilib.dll SSP registration logging plaintext passwords to kiwissp.log; Default Domain Policy set Enabled/Enforced
Rclone renamed lsp.exe with ngconf.txt config staged in pre-existing Defender-excluded folders; Nezha/MeshAgent/Ligolo-ng/Cloudflared for C2

sources.title: Medusa Ransomware Activity Continues to Increase
Medusa Ransomware Uses Malicious Driver to Disable Anti-Malware with Stolen Certificates (ABYSSWORKER, Elastic Security Labs research)

chain.procedure: Exploits unpatched internet-facing software within ~24h of disclosure: ScreenConnect CVE-2024-1709, FortiClient EMS CVE-2023-48788, GoAnywhere MFT CVE-2025-10035, BeyondTrust CVE-2026-1731 and Microsoft Exchange; confirms success by beaconing to Interactsh (oast.site/.pro/.fun) subdomains. Access is also bought from IABs.
